Read apps/monjournal/docs/how/slices/slice-1-data-foundation/slice.md sections 'Technical Scope - Data Models' and 'Implementation Steps 1-2'. Implement the data foundation layer for MonJournal:

1. Create src/models/types.ts with interfaces:
   - Thought: id (UUID string), title (string), content (string), createdAt (number), tags (string[] or empty)
   - Tag: name (string), color (string hex)
   - FilterState: text?, dateStart?, dateEnd?, selectedTags?

2. Create src/models/thoughtModel.ts:
   - Export Thought type
   - Function createThought(title: string, content: string, tags: string[]): Thought
     - Auto-generate UUID for id
     - Set createdAt to current timestamp in ms
     - Ensure immutability (readonly fields in interface)
   - Function validateThought(t: any): boolean
     - Check required fields: id, title, content, createdAt
     - Validate types (id is string, createdAt is number, tags is array)

3. Create src/utils/colorPalette.ts:
   - Export COLORS: string[] with 8-12 distinct hex colors
   - Ensure WCAG AA compliant colors for text contrast
   - Example palette: ["#FF6B6B", "#4ECDC4", "#45B7D1", "#FFA07A", "#98D8C8", "#F7DC6F", "#BB8FCE", "#85C1E2"]

4. Create src/models/tagModel.ts:
   - Export Tag type
   - Function deriveTags(thoughts: Thought[]): Tag[]
     - Collect unique tag names from all thoughts
     - Compute color for each tag using getTagColor()
     - Return array of Tag objects {name, color}
   - Function getTagColor(tagName: string): string
     - Use deterministic hash: charCodeAt(0) % COLORS.length or similar consistent algorithm
     - Return hex color from COLORS array
     - Same tag name always produces same color

5. Create src/utils/filterLogic.ts:
   - Function matchesTextSearch(thought: Thought, query: string): boolean
     - Case-insensitive substring match in title or content
   - Function matchesDateRange(thought: Thought, start: number | null, end: number | null): boolean
     - Inclusive: start <= createdAt <= end
     - Handle null bounds
   - Function matchesTags(thought: Thought, selectedTags: string[]): boolean
     - Empty selectedTags matches all (no filter)
     - Any thought tag in selectedTags list matches (OR logic)
   - Function applyFilters(thoughts: Thought[], filters: FilterState): Thought[]
     - Compose all filters with AND logic
     - Apply text, dateRange, tags filters in sequence

All functions must be pure and stateless. Include JSDoc comments. No React hooks in this file.

Read apps/monjournal/docs/how/slices/slice-1-data-foundation/slice.md sections 'Technical Scope - Modules' (items 4-5). Implement the localStorage persistence layer:

1. Create src/hooks/useLocalStorage.ts (utility hook):
   - Function getItem(key: string): any
     - Read from localStorage, parse JSON, return value
     - Return null if key not found
     - Catch parse errors, log, return null
   - Function setItem(key: string, value: any): void
     - Serialize to JSON and write to localStorage
     - Catch quota exceeded errors, log gracefully
   - Error handling: never throw, always log to console

2. Create src/hooks/useThoughts.ts (React custom hook):
   - Returns object: {
       thoughts: Thought[],
       addThought(thought: Thought): void,
       getTags(): Tag[],
       getThoughts(): Thought[]
     }
   - Implementation:
     - useState to hold thoughts array
     - useEffect: on mount, read from localStorage key "monjournal_thoughts"
     - If missing or corrupt, initialize to empty array []
     - Validate each thought using validateThought() from slice A
     - addThought(t): append to state, call setItem to persist
     - getTags(): call deriveTags(thoughts) and return
     - getThoughts(): return thoughts array
   - LocalStorage schema: store as JSON under key "monjournal_thoughts"
   - Immutability: thoughts array and individual thoughts never mutated

3. Test the hook:
   - Mock localStorage
   - Verify initial load from empty storage
   - Verify addThought persists to localStorage
   - Verify getTags returns derived tags with correct colors
   - Verify corrupted JSON resets to empty array

Dependency: must import types and functions from task A (types.ts, thoughtModel.ts, tagModel.ts, colorPalette.ts)

Read apps/monjournal/docs/how/slices/slice-2-thought-list-display/slice.md section 'Utilities - dateFormat.ts'. Implement date formatting utilities:

1. Create src/utils/dateFormat.ts:
   - Function formatDate(timestamp: number, format: 'relative' | 'absolute'): string
     - Relative format: "2 hours ago", "yesterday", "3 days ago", "1 week ago"
       - Use humanized relative time
       - Implementation: calculate difference in ms, convert to human-readable units
       - Examples: recent times (< 1 min) → "just now", (< 1 hour) → "X minutes ago", same day → "today", yesterday → "yesterday", older → "X days ago"
     - Absolute format: "June 4, 2026" locale-aware (use Intl.DateTimeFormat or similar)
       - Output: Month Day, Year (ISO-like but localized)
       - Consistent formatting across browsers

2. Create src/utils/groupByDate.ts:
   - Function groupThoughtsByDate(thoughts: Thought[]): Map<string, Thought[]>
     - Group thoughts by creation date (normalize to midnight, ignore time)
     - Return Map of [dateKey] → Thought[]
     - dateKey format: "YYYY-MM-DD" for stable grouping
     - Within each group, sort by createdAt descending (newest first within day)
     - Handle edge cases: empty array, single thought, same-day thoughts

3. Test both utilities:
   - formatDate: recent, today, yesterday, week ago, month ago
   - groupByDate: empty array, single thought, multiple thoughts same day, multiple days
   - Verify date keys are stable

No dependencies on other slices. Pure utility functions.

Read apps/monjournal/docs/how/slices/slice-2-thought-list-display/slice.md section 'Components - TagDisplay'. Implement the tag color display component:

1. Create src/components/TagDisplay.tsx (React component):
   - Props: { tags: string[], compact?: boolean }
   - Behavior:
     - Render each tag as a colored chip element
     - Use getTagColor() from task A (tagModel.ts) to compute background color
     - Display tag name with contrasting text color (black or white based on background)
     - Responsive sizing: compact=true for mobile/small layouts, false for desktop
     - Layout: inline flex wrap to handle many tags
   - Styling: 4-8px padding, rounded corners, good WCAG AA text contrast
   - Handle empty tags array gracefully (render nothing)
   - Use AppShell CSS base styles for consistency

2. Unit test:
   - Render with multiple tags, verify all tags displayed
   - Verify getTagColor() called for each tag
   - Verify empty array renders nothing
   - Verify compact prop changes sizing

Dependency: imports getTagColor() from task A (tagModel.ts), types from task A (types.ts). 
No dependency on useThoughts hook.

Read apps/monjournal/docs/how/slices/slice-2-thought-list-display/slice.md section 'Components - ThoughtCard'. Implement the individual thought card component:

1. Create src/components/ThoughtCard.tsx (React component):
   - Props: { thought: Thought, onHighlight?: () => void }
   - Render:
     - Title as card header (bold)
     - Content truncated to ~100 characters with ellipsis if longer
     - Creation date formatted via formatDate(createdAt, 'relative') from task C
     - Tags rendered via TagDisplay component (task D), compact=true
     - Optional highlight/selected state for surprise feature (style with border/background)
   - Styling: card-based layout with padding, border, shadow (from AppShell CSS)
   - Hover state for interactivity
   - Accessibility: semantic HTML, readable font sizes

2. Unit test:
   - Render with various thought lengths, verify truncation
     - Content < 100 chars: no ellipsis
     - Content > 100 chars: truncated with ellipsis
   - Verify date formatting (relative format)
   - Verify tags rendered with TagDisplay
   - Verify onHighlight callback works
   - Snapshot test for card layout

Dependency: imports from task C (dateFormat), task D (TagDisplay), task A (types.Thought).

Read apps/monjournal/docs/how/slices/slice-2-thought-list-display/slice.md section 'Components - ThoughtList'. Implement the main thought list display:

1. Create src/components/ThoughtList.tsx (React component):
   - Props: { thoughts: Thought[], onSurpriseClick?: (thought: Thought) => void }
   - Render:
     - Array of ThoughtCard components (task E) for each thought
     - Sorted by createdAt descending (most recent first)
     - Empty state message: "No thoughts yet. Start by adding a new thought!" if thoughts.length === 0
   - Styling: flex layout, responsive spacing (mobile to desktop)
   - Accessibility: list semantics (<ul>, <li>)

2. Unit test:
   - Render with 0, 1, 5+ thoughts
   - Verify empty state message when no thoughts
   - Verify sort order (descending by createdAt)
   - Verify ThoughtCard rendered for each thought
   - Verify onSurpriseClick passed to cards

Dependency: imports ThoughtCard (task E), types.Thought (task A).

Read apps/monjournal/docs/how/slices/slice-2-thought-list-display/slice.md sections 'Components - TimelineView, TimelineGroup'. Implement timeline grouped view:

1. Create src/components/TimelineGroup.tsx (React sub-component):
   - Props: { date: number, thoughts: Thought[], onSurpriseClick?: (thought: Thought) => void }
   - Render:
     - Day separator header: format date using formatDate(date, 'absolute') from task C ("June 4, 2026")
     - Horizontal line with date label
     - List of ThoughtCard components (task E) for that day
   - Styling: separator with horizontal line, date label centered or left-aligned

2. Create src/components/TimelineView.tsx (React component):
   - Props: { thoughts: Thought[], onSurpriseClick?: (thought: Thought) => void }
   - Render:
     - Use groupThoughtsByDate() from task C to organize thoughts
     - Array of TimelineGroup components (one per day)
     - Groups in reverse chronological order (newest group first)
     - Empty state: "No thoughts yet. Start by adding a new thought!" if thoughts.length === 0
   - Styling: vertical timeline layout, responsive
   - Accessibility: semantic structure

3. Unit test:
   - Render with thoughts from multiple days
   - Verify grouping by date
     - Same day thoughts → single group
     - Different days → multiple groups
   - Verify chronological order (newest first)
   - Verify empty state when no thoughts
   - Verify date formatting in separators
   - Verify ThoughtCard rendered for each thought

Dependency: imports from task C (groupByDate, formatDate), task E (ThoughtCard), task A (types.Thought).

Read apps/monjournal/docs/how/slices/slice-2-thought-list-display/slice.md section 'Components - ViewModeToggle'. Implement view mode switcher:

1. Create src/components/ViewModeToggle.tsx (React component):
   - Props: { currentMode: 'list' | 'timeline', onChange: (mode: 'list' | 'timeline') => void }
   - Render:
     - Two toggle buttons or toggle switch: "List" and "Timeline"
     - Active button/segment highlighted (bold, background color, or border)
     - Click handler calls onChange() with selected mode
     - Label indicating current mode (optional)
   - Styling: segmented control or button group, responsive
   - Accessibility: ARIA labels, keyboard navigation (Tab/Enter)

2. Unit test:
   - Render with different modes, verify active state
   - Verify onClick calls onChange with correct mode
   - Verify toggle switches between modes
   - Verify accessibility attributes (role, aria-labels)

No external dependencies beyond React. Pure UI control.
No dependency on useThoughts or data slices.

Read apps/monjournal/docs/how/slices/slice-2-thought-list-display/slice.md section 'Integration with useThoughts Hook' and slice-3-filtering-search/slice.md section 'Integration with Home Component'. Implement the main home page:

1. Create src/pages/Home.tsx (React page component):
   - Initialize useThoughts() hook (task B) to fetch thoughts
   - Initialize viewMode state: useState('list' | 'timeline')
   - Initialize filterState: useState(FilterState) from task A
   - Handler onViewModeChange(mode): updates viewMode state
   - Handler onFilterChange(filters): updates filterState state
   - Call applyFilters(thoughts, filterState) from task A to get filtered results
   - Render:
     - ViewModeToggle component (task H) with currentMode and onChange
     - ThoughtList (task F) or TimelineView (task G) depending on viewMode
       - Pass filtered thoughts to whichever view is active
     - Pass onSurpriseClick handler (for slice 3)
   - Layout: responsive container, vertical stack

2. Implement onSurpriseClick handler (placeholder for slice 3):
   - For now: select random thought from filteredThoughts
   - Calculate: randomIndex = Math.floor(Math.random() * filteredThoughts.length)
   - Return thought at that index
   - Highlight or scroll into view (implementation TBD in slice 3)

3. Unit/integration test:
   - Verify useThoughts() hook is initialized
   - Verify viewMode toggle switches views
   - Verify filters are applied in real-time
   - Verify filtered thoughts passed to active view
   - Verify ThoughtList and TimelineView render correctly

Dependency: imports useThoughts (task B), ViewModeToggle (task H), ThoughtList (task F), TimelineView (task G), applyFilters (task A), types (task A).

Read apps/monjournal/docs/how/slices/slice-3-filtering-search/slice.md section 'Components - FilterPanel, DateRangePicker, TagMultiSelect'. Implement the filter UI:

1. Create src/components/DateRangePicker.tsx (React sub-component):
   - Props: { dateStart: number | null, dateEnd: number | null, onChange: (start: number | null, end: number | null) => void }
   - Render: two HTML <input type="date"> fields
     - Labels: "From:" and "To:"
     - Allow clearing dates (empty field = null)
     - On change: parse date, call onChange with timestamps in ms
   - Validation: warn if start > end
   - No hard error, but visual indication

2. Create src/components/TagMultiSelect.tsx (React sub-component):
   - Props: { availableTags: Tag[], selectedTags: string[], onChange: (selectedTags: string[]) => void }
   - Render:
     - List of checkboxes or toggle buttons, one per tag
     - Use TagDisplay from task D to show colored indicators
     - Selected state clearly indicated (checked checkbox or highlighted button)
     - Click to toggle: add/remove from selectedTags
     - Call onChange with updated array
   - Layout: flex wrap or grid to handle many tags (10+, 100+)
   - Styling: responsive, accessible

3. Create src/components/FilterPanel.tsx (React component):
   - Props: { existingTags: Tag[], onFilterChange: (filters: FilterState) => void, onSurpriseClick: () => void }
   - Local state: { text, dateStart, dateEnd, selectedTags }
   - Render:
     - Text search input: placeholder "Search title and content"
     - DateRangePicker sub-component
     - TagMultiSelect sub-component
     - "Surprise!" button, disabled if no results available
     - Optional "Clear Filters" button
     - Layout: responsive (vertical stack on mobile, horizontal on desktop)
   - Handlers:
     - onTextChange: update text state, call onFilterChange
     - onDateChange: update dateStart/dateEnd, call onFilterChange
     - onTagChange: update selectedTags, call onFilterChange
     - onSurpriseClick: call parent handler
     - onClearFilters: reset all state, call onFilterChange with empty FilterState
   - Styling: form layout from AppShell CSS, responsive

4. Unit test:
   - FilterPanel: renders all controls, calls onFilterChange on input
   - DateRangePicker: parses dates, validates bounds, handles null
   - TagMultiSelect: renders all tags, toggles selection, calls onChange
   - All handlers work correctly

Dependency: imports TagDisplay (task D), types (task A).

Read apps/monjournal/docs/how/slices/slice-4-add-thought-form/slice.md sections 'Overview, Technical Scope - Components, Data Flow'. Implement the add thought form:

1. Create src/components/TagInput.tsx (React controlled input component):
   - Props: { value: string, onChange: (text: string) => void, suggestions: string[], onAddTag: (tag: string) => void, disabled?: boolean }
   - Render:
     - Text input field
     - Dropdown with suggestions filtered by current input (case-insensitive substring)
     - On Enter key: add tag if input is non-empty and not duplicate
     - On suggestion click: add tag
     - Clear input after tag is added
   - Styling: input + dropdown suggestion list

2. Create src/components/TagList.tsx (React component):
   - Props: { tags: string[], onRemoveTag: (tag: string) => void }
   - Render:
     - Each tag as colored chip with background from getTagColor() (task A)
     - Display tag name and remove button (X)
     - Click remove: call onRemoveTag(tag)
   - Styling: inline flex chips with colors
   - Handle empty array gracefully

3. Create src/pages/AddThought.tsx (React page component):
   - State:
     - title: string
     - content: string
     - selectedTags: string[]
     - tagInput: string (for TagInput controlled value)
     - errors: { title?: string, content?: string } (validation)
     - isSubmitting: boolean (prevent duplicate submissions)
   - Initialize useThoughts() to get existing tags
   - Render:
     - Title: "Add a New Thought"
     - Title input field (required)
     - Content textarea (required)
     - TagInput component with suggestions from getTags()
     - TagList showing selected tags
     - Cancel and Save buttons
   - Handlers:
     - onTitleChange: update title, clear error
     - onContentChange: update content, clear error
     - onAddTag: add to selectedTags, clear tagInput
     - onRemoveTag: remove from selectedTags
     - onTagInputChange: update tagInput
     - onSave: validate title/content, create Thought via createThought(), call useThoughts.addThought(), show success message, redirect to /
     - onCancel: clear form or navigate back
   - Validation:
     - Title required, non-empty, non-whitespace
     - Content required, non-empty, non-whitespace
     - Show inline error messages
     - Debounce validation (500ms)
   - Styling: form layout from AppShell CSS, responsive
   - Accessibility: keyboard navigation (Enter to submit), form labels

4. Unit/integration test:
   - Form renders all inputs
   - Validation prevents submission if title/content empty
   - addThought() called with correct data on save
   - Navigation to / on successful save
   - TagInput autocomplete works
   - TagList displays and removes tags correctly

Dependency: imports useThoughts (task B), createThought, getTagColor (task A), types (task A), TagInput, TagList from this file.

Read apps/monjournal/docs/how/architecture.md section '5. Routing with React Router'. Wire up routing and integrate all slices:

1. Update src/App.tsx (main app component):
   - Ensure React Router is configured from AppShell
   - Add routes:
     - Path "/" → Home component (task I)
     - Path "/add" → AddThought component (task K)
     - Keep any existing AppShell routes (/about, etc)
   - Verify Layout component wraps routes (from AppShell)
   - Import all page components (Home, AddThought)

2. Update navigation links (in AppShell Layout/Header):
   - Verify "Home" link points to "/"
   - Verify "Add Thought" link points to "/add"
   - Use React Router Link component

3. Verify integration:
   - Home page renders FilterPanel (task J) + ViewModeToggle (task H) + ThoughtList/TimelineView
   - AddThought page accessible via /add route
   - Navigation between pages works
   - All imports are correct (no circular dependencies)
   - TypeScript compiles without errors

4. Run app and verify:
   - npm run dev starts without errors
   - Home page loads with empty thoughts (localStorage integration)
   - Can navigate to /add
   - Can add a thought (basic flow)
   - New thought appears on home page

5. No unit tests required for this file (integration verification via app run).

Dependency: integrates all tasks (A-K).
